messages:
Sara: FYI — customer `acme-corp` escalated. They say KMS access events are missing from their audit export for the outage window (2026-02-28 02:00-02:30 UTC). Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/4521. Can security confirm scope and whether we need to notify?
Anita: copying in @James. Quick Qs: which key IDs did they query, and did they pull raw audit S3 or our UI export? Also, did Dedicated vs Hosted differ for that tenant?
Sara: they attached UI export csv and one key id: `projects/acme/keys/kms-us-01`. It looks like no rows with `kms_access` for that half hour. They are hosted customers.
audit-bot: automated note — audit indices: `audit-logs-*`. Retention: 90 days for `audit.kms_access`. Backups to long-term: enabled. Query hint: `index:audit-logs-* AND event:kms_access AND timestamp:[2026-02-28T02:00 TO 2026-02-28T02:30]`.
James: thanks. First take: need to confirm (1) whether events were generated but filtered in UI export, (2) if logs were ingested at time of incident, or delayed. Anita — can you run the ES query and check ingest timestamps + shard delays? Also include HSM key-op logs if available.
Anita: running now. GS query I used: ```GET /audit-logs-*/_search
{
  "query": {
    "bool": {
      "must": [
        {"term": {"event":"kms_access"}},
        {"term": {"resource.key_id":"projects/acme/keys/kms-us-01"}},
        {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "2026-02-28T02:00:00Z", "lte": "2026-02-28T02:30:00Z"}}}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```
Sara: thanks — let us know quick. Customer is asking if this is a compliance gap.
Anita: partial result: found 3 ingest events but with `ingest.timestamp` of 2026-02-28T02:45:12Z (delayed by ~15m). Sample hit: `{"@timestamp":"2026-02-28T02:03:11Z","event":"kms_access","resource.key_id":"projects/acme/keys/kms-us-01","actor":"svc-gateway"}`. Also a couple of HSM audit lines linking to `hsm-node-3` but no outbound egress.
James: good catch — looks like logs were generated but ingestion lagged during the outage (queueing + shard pressure). That means audit data existed at source and was not dropped. No evidence of key material export.
Leo: from legal: if logs existed and no exfiltration, we should still provide a factual timeline to the customer within 48 hours and offer the exported logs. If any customer-sensitive PII was exposed in logs, we handle differently — but seems not the case.
Devon: is this a docs / SLA issue? We may want to note that UI export can miss delayed-ingested entries if export snapshot was taken during the outage. Do we need to update export docs?
James: action items: (1) Anita to produce a time-ordered export for the customer's key for the window and attach to ticket (anon as needed). (2) Support to notify customer with timeline + attach logs. (3) Ops to investigate ingestion lag root cause and mitigation. (4) Legal to review notification draft.
Anita: working on the export now — will put a sanitized CSV in the ticket. ETA 2 hours.
Sara: Roger. I'll draft the customer note once export is in. Draft will include: timeline, confirmation logs generated, no evidence of external access, and steps we're taking (ingest backlog fix + monitoring).
James: thumbs up. If legal wants wording, loop Leo. :thumbsup:
Leo: I'll review the draft when ready. Recommend we include an offer for a third-party audit export if they request.
Devon: created a follow-up issue for docs/SLA: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/1287 — tagging for product review.
Sara: thanks team. I'll update ticket 4521 and ping customer after export attached. :white_check_mark:
